title: Greenlight Takes a Digital Wall Calendar and Adds My Most-Wanted Feature
gist: Wired reviews the $299 Greenlight Family Hub, a digital wall calendar that is rare in including an AI voice assistant (behind a $10-a-month Family Hub+ membership), noting its overly sensitive wake word and Big Brother-ish tracking features. The author asks why Skylight and Amazon have not added voice to calendars or calendar modes to smart displays; both declined comment.

insights.claim: Digital wall calendars have grown in popularity this year, driven by the Skylight Calendar, by consolidating Google, iCalendar and Outlook calendars on one home device.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: A new smart-home device category with a clear leader.
insights.locator: Digital wall calendars have been on the rise in popularity this year

insights.claim: Skylight's business model has become charging for storage on both its calendars and digital photo frames, including the photo screen saver feature that Greenlight offers without a subscription.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Recurring-revenue models differ across competitors, a competitive axis.
insights.locator: Skylight’s business model in general has become charging for storage

insights.claim: The Greenlight Family Hub (15.6 inch, $299, discounted to $279 with Family Hub+) extends the company's banking tool for parents and teens into a platform for calendars, chores, kids' spending and family location tracking.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Greenlight uses the calendar as a distribution wedge for its existing fintech and family offerings.
insights.locator: Greenlight grew from a banking tool

insights.claim: Greenlight puts its AI assistant, voice interaction and family location sharing behind a $10-a-month membership while most other features are free.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Subscription upsell on AI features is the monetization path in this category.
insights.quote: But there’s one feature behind the paywall (a $10-a-month membership)
insights.locator: But there’s one feature behind the paywall

insights.claim: Greenlight chief product officer Sushil Sharma says the company noticed voice support was absent in the digital calendar market and built it in to create an all-in-one command center that limits the number of devices families need.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Voice is positioned as a differentiator against calendar-only rivals.
insights.locator: Greenlight says it noticed the lack of voice support

insights.claim: The assistant uses frontier large language models with Greenlight's proprietary safety tools designed for families, shows a conversation panel similar to Alexa+ on Echo Show, and has a microphone but no camera.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Family-safety layers on top of third-party LLMs are a template for kid-oriented AI products.
insights.locator: Greenlight says its family AI assistant uses frontier large language models

insights.claim: The Greenlight hub wakes randomly on its "Hey Greenlight" wake phrase and keeps listening for follow-ups, so it tries to answer ordinary household conversation, a problem the author says is common to AI-powered voice assistants including her Gemini speaker.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Always-listening AI assistants have unresolved false-trigger and privacy friction.
insights.locator: Greenlight’s Hub is supposed to only wake at its wake phrase

insights.claim: The author says the Family Hub's location, finance and microphone features can feel Big Brother-like, and that a setup bug forced her into a child's financial pathway until support cleared her information.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Setup bugs and data scope are adoption risks for bundled family platforms.

themes.theme: Market gap: voice in calendars and calendar in smart displays

insights.claim: Amazon and Skylight declined to comment on why neither offers a voice-enabled calendar or calendar mode, and the author speculates cost and hardware changes for Skylight while saying Amazon is well positioned, though Alexa+ is already paywalled.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: A possible product opening for Amazon or Skylight to merge calendar and smart-display categories.
insights.locator: I reached out to both Amazon and Skylight

insights.claim: The author notes smart displays have lacked full-page calendar features and that Apple just announced its first smart display.
insights.speaker: Nena Farrell
insights.so_what: Apple's entry could reshape the smart-display category.
insights.locator: Smart displays have existed for years
